subject: maths
topic: Mensuration: perimeter, area, volume and surface area

kept.q: A square garden in Kano has each side measuring 15 m. What is the perimeter of the garden?
kept.explanation: A square has 4 equal sides, so perimeter = 4 x side = 4 x 15 = 60 m.
kept.pidgin: Square get 4 equal sides, so perimeter na 4 x side = 4 x 15 = 60 m.

kept.q: A rectangular water tank in a school hostel has length 2.5 m, width 2 m and height 1.6 m. Calculate the volume of the tank in cubic metres.
kept.explanation: Volume of a cuboid = length x width x height = 2.5 x 2 x 1.6 = 8.0 m^3. This is the amount of water the tank can hold.
kept.pidgin: Volume of cuboid na length x width x height = 2.5 x 2 x 1.6 = 8.0 m^3. Na so much water the tank fit hold.

kept.q: A spherical ball used for a school sports event has radius 10.5 cm. Find its total surface area. (Take pi = 22/7)
kept.explanation: Surface area of a sphere = 4 x pi x r^2 = 4 x (22/7) x 10.5^2 = 4 x (22/7) x 110.25 = 1386 cm^2.
kept.pidgin: Surface area of sphere na 4 x pi x r^2 = 4 x (22/7) x 10.5^2 = 4 x (22/7) x 110.25 = 1386 cm^2.

kept.q: A metal bucket has the shape of a frustum of a cone. Its top radius is 14 cm, its bottom radius is 7 cm, and its height is 24 cm. Calculate the volume of the bucket. (Take pi = 22/7)
kept.pidgin: Volume of frustum na (1/3) x pi x h x (R^2 + Rr + r^2). Here R=14, r=7, h=24, so V = (1/3) x (22/7) x 24 x (196+98+49) = 8624 cm^3.
